audience_description: A SaaS founder, product manager, or growth marketer at a mid-market or enterprise company who wants to understand how Webflow repositioned itself from a designer tool to an enterprise marketing platform—specifically to inform their own positioning strategy, pricing model evolution, or AI/automation narrative.
recommended_h1_format: [Company] Homepage Teardown: How It Shifted From No-Code Builder to Enterprise Growth Platform
content_angle: Focus on the strategic *why* behind the repositioning—not just the cosmetic changes. The searcher wants to understand: (1) Why Webflow abandoned the 'democratize code' narrative for 'growth engine'; (2) How the shift from 'Get started free' to 'Contact Sales' signals a move upmarket; (3) What 'AEO' positioning teaches about claiming a new category; (4) Whether this playbook applies to their own SaaS. This is about learning a repositioning playbook, not admiring design changes.
what_the_searcher_wants: To reverse-engineer a high-stakes repositioning decision (from SMB/designer market to enterprise) so they can evaluate whether a similar strategy makes sense for their company, or to understand the signals that indicate when a product should shift its narrative and buyer.
what_to_avoid: Avoid treating this as a visual design critique or pixel-by-pixel walkthrough. The searcher does not care that the button color changed or the layout is cleaner. They *will* bounce if you don't explain the business logic: Why did Webflow need to move upmarket? What was the growth ceiling at the designer level? How does 'AEO' solve a real buyer problem versus being marketing theater? Avoid generic praise ('great design,' 'clear messaging') without connecting it to a business outcome or positioning principle.
